content:
Below are the four new files — two per environment, added independently since this arm has no shared base.

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  namespace: myapp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    environment: dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
# Grants the existing dev service-account User (see dev/iam.yaml) object-level
# access to the logs bucket only. Kept as a separate managed Policy + attachment
# so the assets-bucket policy in dev/iam.yaml is untouched.
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  namespace: myapp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    environment: dev
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  description: Read/write objects in myapp-logs-dev only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

If your `dev/iam.yaml` `User` lists its policies inline via `spec.policies`, add
`arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:policy/myapp-logs-access-dev` to that list instead of
using the attachment below.

`dev/logs-policy-attachment.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  # Same name as the User declared in dev/iam.yaml — this file only adds the
  # logs policy ARN to its policies list. If you prefer a single source of
  # truth, merge this policies entry into dev/iam.yaml and delete this file.
  name: myapp-sa-dev
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-sa-dev
  policies:
    - arn:aws:iam::111111111111:policy/myapp-assets-access-dev
    - arn:aws:iam::111111111111:policy/myapp-logs-access-dev
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  namespace: myapp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    environment: prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
# Grants the existing prod service-account Role (see prod/iam.yaml) object-level
# access to the logs bucket only. No wildcard actions, no wildcard resources.
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  namespace: myapp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
    environment: prod
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  description: Read/write objects in myapp-logs-prod only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`prod/logs-policy-attachment.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  # Same name as the Role declared in prod/iam.yaml (OIDC trust policy lives
  # there and is unchanged). This file only adds the logs policy ARN.
  name: myapp-sa-prod
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-sa-prod
  policies:
    - arn:aws:iam::222222222222:policy/myapp-assets-access-prod
    - arn:aws:iam::222222222222:policy/myapp-logs-access-prod
```

Notes:

- Replace the placeholder account IDs (`111111111111`, `222222222222`) with your
  real dev/prod account IDs, and the existing assets policy ARNs with whatever
  is currently listed in each `iam.yaml`. The attachment files must repeat the
  full `policies` list because `kubectl apply` replaces the field wholesale —
  omitting the assets ARN would revoke assets access.
- Cleanest alternative: skip the two `*-policy-attachment.yaml` files entirely
  and append the logs policy ARN directly to the `policies` list in
  `dev/iam.yaml` and `prod/iam.yaml`. That avoids two objects fighting over the
  same `spec.policies` field.
- If your ACK IAM controller version exposes `Resource` only as a string, the
  documents above are already single-string form; a list (`["arn:...:/*"]`) is
  equally valid.
- The `dev/` and `prod/` edits are fully duplicated by design: applying
  `kubectl apply -f dev/` touches nothing in prod, and vice versa. The cost of
  this arm is exactly that duplication — four resource definitions where a
  shared base would need one bucket template and one policy template.
- Neither policy references `arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-*`, so assets-bucket
  access is unchanged. Neither grants `s3:ListBucket`; add it on the bucket ARN
  (without `/*`) only if the application actually enumerates objects.
